nodes.content: Predict specific protein molecular functions in unseen families while distinguishing genuine functional novelty from incomplete annotations.
requirements: Achieve ≥10% relative macro-AUPRC improvement over sequence-only transfer on family-disjoint, temporally held-out annotations.
Distinguish novel functions from missing annotations with ≥0.80 AUROC on independently adjudicated proteins.

nodes.content: Combine ESM-2 embeddings and Foldseek active-site matches for GO prediction; distinguish novelty from annotation gaps using assay-coverage-aware positive-unlabeled calibration.
Can assay-coverage estimates distinguish untested GO activities from genuinely novel functions when active-site matches lack matching annotations?
For proteins with unlabeled active-site matches, assay-coverage-aware calibration will distinguish genuine novelty from annotation gaps at AUROC ≥0.80.
On 400 independently adjudicated proteins with unlabeled Foldseek active-site matches, compare assay-coverage-calibrated versus uncalibrated novelty-versus-gap AUROC.
Across 400 independently adjudicated proteins with unlabeled active-site matches, assay-coverage calibration raised novelty-versus-gap AUROC from 0.72 to 0.84.
Retain assay-coverage calibration for novelty triage because adjudicated AUROC reached 0.84, exceeding the 0.80 target.
Retain calibration; train through 2024, then compare Foldseek–ESM-2 against sequence-only macro-AUPRC on Pfam-disjoint 2025–2026 GO annotations.
Train Foldseek–ESM-2 and sequence-only baselines on pre-2025 annotations; measure macro-AUPRC on Pfam-disjoint 2025–2026 experimental GO additions.
PfamTime-GO v1 contains frozen Pfam-disjoint splits, 2025–2026 experimental labels, both models’ predictions, and macro-AUPRC evaluation scripts.
Audit PfamTime-GO v1 for split leakage, then bootstrap its predictions to test ≥10% relative macro-AUPRC improvement.
PfamTime-GO v1 had no cross-split Pfam overlaps; Foldseek–ESM-2 macro-AUPRC was 0.284 versus sequence-only 0.250 (+13.6%).
Among proteins with unlabeled active-site matches, assay-provenance coverage outperforms annotation-count coverage by ≥0.08 novelty-versus-gap AUROC.
On the 400 adjudicated proteins with unlabeled active-site matches, compare assay-provenance and annotation-count coverage via paired cross-validated AUROC.
On 400 adjudicated proteins, assay-provenance coverage reached novelty-versus-gap AUROC 0.84 versus annotation-count coverage 0.79, a 0.05 gain.
Does Foldseek–ESM-2’s macro-AUPRC gain persist for rare catalytic GO terms, or arise mainly from broadly annotated binding functions?
Stratify PfamTime-GO v1 catalytic and binding terms by ≤20 training positives; bootstrap relative macro-AUPRC gains from frozen predictions.
Partition PfamTime-GO v1 terms by catalytic versus binding function and training frequency; bootstrap macro-AUPRC gains across held-out families.
PfamTime-GO v1 stratification report contains catalytic and binding term lists, ≤20-positive rare-term flags, and family-bootstrap macro-AUPRC comparisons.
Train a GO-hierarchy-aware reaction graph on ligand-binding pockets and verified substrates, with assay-coverage-calibrated novelty abstention.
Can pre-2025 substrate–reaction edges improve substrate-specific GO prediction in unseen Pfam families without leaking held-out annotations?
Leakage-filtered pre-2025 substrate–reaction edges will increase substrate-specific GO macro-AUPRC ≥10% over Foldseek–ESM-2 on held-out Pfam families.
Use the PfamTime-GO stratification report to select catalytic terms; leakage-filter pre-2025 reaction edges and compare substrate-specific macro-AUPRC against Foldseek–ESM-2.
On held-out Pfam families, leakage-filtered reaction edges raised substrate-specific GO macro-AUPRC from 0.214 to 0.221 (+3.3%), below 10%.
For high-confidence ligand pockets, pre-2025 verified substrate–reaction edges will improve substrate-specific macro-AUPRC ≥10% over Foldseek–ESM-2.
Using PfamTime-GO stratification, bootstrap pre-2025 verified-edge versus Foldseek–ESM-2 substrate-specific macro-AUPRC across held-out families with pocket pLDDT ≥90.
For held-out families with pocket pLDDT ≥90, verified-edge macro-AUPRC was 0.243 versus Foldseek–ESM-2’s 0.230 (+5.7%).
Using PfamTime-GO catalytic strata, retest verified-edge versus Foldseek–ESM-2 macro-AUPRC on 2026-only Pfam-disjoint proteins with pocket pLDDT ≥90.
On 2026-only Pfam-disjoint proteins with pocket pLDDT ≥90, verified edges achieved substrate-specific macro-AUPRC 0.224 versus 0.200 (+12%).
After leakage audits, verified substrate edges yield ≥10% macro-AUPRC improvement in 2026-only high-confidence pockets, but not pooled families.
Using PfamTime-GO strata, audit pre-2025 edge provenance; bootstrap macro-AUPRC gains versus Foldseek–ESM-2 across pooled and 2026-only pLDDT ≥90 pockets.
Edge-provenance audit found zero held-out annotation links; pLDDT ≥90 pockets gained 12% macro-AUPRC in 2026-only versus 5.7% pooled.
Defer broad reaction-graph deployment; pilot verified-edge reranking on 2026-only pLDDT ≥90 pockets, pending replication of its 12% gain.
Replicate the verified-edge pilot on independent 2026-only Pfam-disjoint proteins with pocket pLDDT ≥90; audit provenance and compare macro-AUPRC.
Freeze an independent 2026-only Pfam-disjoint cohort with pocket pLDDT ≥90; audit edge provenance and bootstrap verified-edge versus Foldseek–ESM-2 macro-AUPRC.
PocketRep-2026 v1 contains independent Pfam-disjoint 2026 proteins, pLDDT ≥90 pocket masks, edge-provenance audits, and bootstrap macro-AUPRC comparisons.
Fuse conserved operon neighborhoods and knockout phenotypes through cross-genome graph attention; calibrate novelty predictions with verified negative assays.
Do conserved operon neighborhoods improve specific GO predictions across unseen families independently of taxonomic relatedness and annotation density?
Conserved operon attention will improve family-disjoint GO macro-AUPRC ≥10% over Foldseek–ESM-2 after matching taxa and annotation density.
Using PocketRep-2026 v1 proteins, assemble conserved operon graphs and compare GO macro-AUPRC against Foldseek–ESM-2 after taxon and annotation-density matching.
On taxon- and annotation-density-matched PocketRep-2026 proteins, operon attention raised GO macro-AUPRC from 0.230 to 0.258 (+12.2%).
Test operon attention on clade-held-out, annotation-density-matched PocketRep-2026 proteins; mask neighbor annotations and compare macro-AUPRC after operon-edge ablation.
Construct genus-held-out PocketRep-2026 splits; match annotation density, mask neighbor GO labels, and compare operon attention against edge ablation by macro-AUPRC.
OperonHoldout-2026 v1 contains genus-held-out splits, matched annotation-density strata, masked-neighbor predictions, and operon-edge ablation macro-AUPRC scripts.
Audit OperonHoldout-2026 v1 for leakage; bootstrap genus-held-out macro-AUPRC for operon attention, edge ablation, and Foldseek–ESM-2.
OperonHoldout-2026 passed leakage audits; genus-held-out macro-AUPRC was 0.236 versus 0.209 for Foldseek–ESM-2 and 0.211 after edge ablation.
